clue.text: Brummie's view of football club's getting international prestige finally?

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: City is a common football club name, here with its possessive S
a cap is awarded for each international appearance
the final letter of prestige

explanation.surface: The Birmingham setter asks whether a football club gains a reputation abroad in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Brummie is the setter, and a Brummie lives in the city of Birmingham, so the opening words define the answer by pointing at the setter's own urban outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A cityscape is an urban view, such as a Birmingham native would see from home.

clue.text: Wound one's seen on butt of snake charmer

indicators.note: the butt is the tail end, so take the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: a cut is a wound
Roman numeral one
the tail letter of snake

explanation.surface: A snake charmer has been bitten or cut on the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake charmer' reads as one phrase, but charmer stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive, appealing person, someone who charms.

clue.text: Figure getting fit can be supported

blocks.note: ten is a number, a figure
fit as in capable

explanation.surface: Someone's physique improving might be something you can endorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be defended or maintained in argument.

clue.text: Beat time, frantically following soprano

indicators.note: frantic action is wild and disordered, so the letters lose their order
following places the reworked word after the next item

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A singer beats time in a frenzy behind the soprano, like an anxious conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat time' looks like a musical phrase, but Beat alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To smite is to strike hard, an old-fashioned verb for hitting.

clue.text: Very good name in Gaelic rum

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the letters come out oddly ordered

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-behaved name for a rum in the Gaelic language.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum looks like the drink; here it is the old adjective meaning peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic behaviour is saintly, extremely well behaved, like an angel.

clue.text: Key Republicans' focus after senate is disrupted

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown out of order, so those letters get rearranged
a focus is the central point, so take the middle letter of the word
after places this letter behind the rearranged group

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
the central letter of the eleven-letter Republicans

explanation.surface: American politics: the Republicans concentrate on what matters while the Senate is in turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Something key is crucial or indispensable, which is what essential means.

clue.text: The point of putting sulphur in container

indicators.note: putting one thing in another means placing it inside

blocks.note: a cup is a container
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the purpose is of putting sulphur in a vessel, as in a chemistry lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The point of' reads as 'the purpose of'; the definition is a literal point.
explanation.definitionFit: A cusp is a pointed end, as where two curves meet or the tip of a tooth.

clue.text: As Cream might be producing record including set by The Void

indicators.note: a void word is emptied of its insides, so only its outer letters survive
by means next to, placing one piece beside the other
including means holding the following material inside

blocks.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record
a lot is a set of items, as at auction
the outside letters of The

explanation.surface: A rock music in-joke: Cream, the 1960s band, recording a set alongside a band called The Void.
explanation.walkthrough: Cream was Eric Clapton's 1960s rock trio, which makes the capitalised Cream look like the band; the definition means clotted cream, a thick Devon and Cornwall cream served with scones.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotted cream is thickened by slow heating, so cream may be described as clotted.

clue.text: Lead soldier's cap put with fruit and nut

indicators.note: a cap sits on top, so take the first letter of the word

blocks.note: the opening letter of soldier
a pear is a fruit
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: An infantryman wears a helmet stuffed with fruit and nuts: a ration-pack image.
explanation.walkthrough: Nut is a slang word for the head, as in 'use your nut'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead a campaign is to lead it from the front.

clue.text: Putting up with enduring British group, aged rock symbols

blocks.note: standing something means tolerating it
the Rolling Stones, a British band going for over sixty years

explanation.surface: Tolerating a long-lived British band of ageing rock stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aged rock symbols' looks like a dig at elderly rock musicians, but means prehistoric stones such as Stonehenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing stones are ancient upright monoliths, old rocks with ritual or symbolic meaning.

clue.text: See 8
Remuneration down under initially lacking for poor

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
lacking means going without, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a fee is payment for a service
feeling down is feeling blue
the opening letter of under

explanation.surface: Payment in Australia is thin at first for the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' reads as Australia, but the two words split: down is a mood, and under only supplies its first letter to be removed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble and poor both describe something weak or inadequate in quality.

clue.text: Enduring, so it seems to jaded scholars?

definitions.text: so it seems to jaded scholars

blocks.note: first meaning: lasting a long while

blocks.clueFragment: so it seems to jaded scholars
blocks.note: second meaning: bored pupils find the school term drags on

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a whimsical reading: to tired students every academic term feels long.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-term arrangement is one that lasts or endures over an extended period.

clue.text: Cast encasing top of leg for protection

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter in an across clue
encasing means wrapping around something else

blocks.note: shied is a past tense of shy, to throw
the opening letter of leg

explanation.surface: A plaster cast around the upper leg protects a broken limb.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast looks like a plaster cast; it is a verb meaning threw.
explanation.definitionFit: A shield is something held up or placed to protect against harm.

clue.text: Spirit produced by tramp dropping round – proceed to get drunk almost

indicators.note: dropping means letting something go, so one letter leaves
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a hobo is a tramp
O is round in shape
go means proceed
blind is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: A drink-sodden tramp heads off to get almost paralytic on spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit suggests liquor amid all the drinking, but means a goblin-like sprite; Hobgoblin is also a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobgoblin is a mischievous imp or sprite from folklore, a kind of spirit.

clue.text: Cardinal possibly turns up with replica gun

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: cardinal is a shade of red, possibly indicating an example
a ringer, as in dead ringer, is an exact lookalike

explanation.surface: A cardinal arrives carrying a fake pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal looks like a churchman; here it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket pistol, named after its American maker.

clue.text: Issue's chapter 1: 'Leader's short measure'

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for chapter
Roman numeral one
LDR is the short form of leader
an en is a printer's measure

explanation.surface: A magazine issue's first chapter is titled 'Leader's short measure'.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue reads as a magazine number, but it is the legal word for offspring. An en is a printing unit of width.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal and legal term for offspring, a person's children.

clue.text: Shades of old book's remedies

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
B for book, with its possessive S
cures are remedies

explanation.surface: Ghosts haunting an old book of folk remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: Shades looks like a noun, ghosts or hues; it is a verb meaning covers in shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: To shade something and to obscure it both mean to hide it from view or darken it.

clue.text: One who's in the nick of time after politician Vera, investigating corruption, starts

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters of each of the preceding words
after puts the time letter behind the rest

blocks.note: Con is short for a Conservative politician
the first letters of these three words
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A detective, Vera, starts investigating political corruption just in time to catch a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the nick of time' is a fixed phrase, but the definition stops at nick, British slang for prison. Vera is a British TV detective series.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict is a person serving a prison sentence, someone locked up in jail.

clue.text: As this should be very large, blue novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new form

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
L is the abbreviation for large
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A very large blue novel, as this one should be: an author's ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' is the clue itself: every crossword clue ought to be solvable.
explanation.definitionFit: Soluble means able to be solved, which a fair crossword clue should always be.

clue.text: A dear daughter and a Greek character

blocks.note: a lamb, a term for a sweet and dear person
D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lovely daughter and a lovable Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling someone 'a lamb' means they are a dear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in that script.

clue.text: Police force hosting broadcast about Glasgow's top detective

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
about means going round, so one piece wraps another
a host holds guests within, so this piece goes around the rest

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
to air something is to broadcast it
the opening letter of Glasgow

explanation.surface: A police force puts on a programme about the leading detective in Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasgow points to a Scottish detective such as Taggart, but the sleuth is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Maigret is Georges Simenon's fictional Paris police detective.

clue.text: Decline to go this way

blocks.note: first meaning: a downward slope, as a noun
second meaning: the direction things travel when they deteriorate

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as refusing to take a route; the two halves are a noun for a slope and the idiom for getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A downhill is a descending slope, and to go downhill is an idiom meaning to deteriorate.

clue.text: One pound tucked into crack headwear

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside something else

blocks.note: a crack is an attempt, a try
Roman numeral one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A pound coin slipped into the band of a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack looks like a split; it means a go, as in 'have a crack at it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with an indented crown, a form of headwear.

clue.text: It's symbolic of male bear taking precedence

indicators.note: taking precedence means coming first, so the second word leads the first

blocks.note: to tote is to carry or bear
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A male bear standing first represents something, as on a carved pole.
explanation.walkthrough: Bear reads as the animal, which fits a totem pole; it is a verb meaning carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem, an object or animal treated as a symbol of a clan.

clue.text: Spartan language, technically

blocks.note: first meaning: plain, without frills
second meaning: an early computer programming language

explanation.walkthrough: Spartan suggests ancient Greek speech, but it means austere; technically signals the computing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means simple and minimal, and BASIC is a beginner's computer programming language.

clue.text: Cathedral supporter is nevertheless into very short hair

indicators.note: into means going inside, so this word sits within the phrase

blocks.note: flying as in a flying visit, one that is very brief
but means nevertheless
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A cathedral's backer still has a crew cut, despite the robes.
explanation.walkthrough: The conjunction goes between the two halves of the phrase for a very brief lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying buttress is an arched exterior support propping up the walls of a Gothic cathedral.

clue.text: See 24
Old King Cole's chief fan

indicators.note: the chief letter is the head one, the first

blocks.note: the opening letter of Cole
a nut is an enthusiast, as in fitness nut

explanation.surface: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme has a devoted admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is a nursery-rhyme monarch, so the definition hides in a familiar phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Cnut was an eleventh-century king of England, Denmark and Norway, also called Canute.

clue.text: Characteristic of a puffed joint?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cannabis cigarette that has been smoked
setter's reading: describing a swollen, inflamed knee or knuckle

explanation.walkthrough: Puffed joint points to drug-smoking; the real joint is a body part, puffed meaning swollen.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatic describes the painful inflammation and swelling of joints and muscles.
